transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Amara Singh (Solstice Head of ML), Priya Rao (Prod), Diego Morales (SRE)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on POC quality evaluation playbook: golden prompts, regression set, hallucination checks, scoring rubric, workload sizing for bench runs, and timeline to pilot. AE + two SEs from Redwood; Solstice product + ML + SRE represented. Conversation covered acceptance criteria (latency & precision thresholds), what counts as hallucination for Solstice, data residency and sampling, and logistics for running benchmarks in Redwood hosted/dedicated modes.

Topics covered:
- Success criteria (functional accuracy, hallucination tolerance, latency targets)
- Golden prompt set and augmentation rules
- Regression test design and pass/fail thresholds
- Format and schema validation checks (structured outputs)
- Workload sizing for bench (qps, concurrency, avg tokens)
- Timeline and next steps

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see you all. we'll run for about 45-ish minutes, hopefully have clear next steps. amara, priya, diego, are you good on time?
[00:14] Amara: yes yep, thanks maya. we've got about an hour, that's fine.
[00:21] Priya: fine here.
[00:24] Diego: all good.
[00:27] Ravi: cool, i'll jump in on the technical bits later. high level today is to align on what you want to measure in the poc -- accuracy / hallucination / latency / cost tradeoffs.

[00:45] Amara: great. quick context: we run a customer support summarization + action-extraction pipeline, about 12k daily requests, spikes to 120 rps during business hours. main concerns are hallucination in action extraction (we can't surface incorrect actions to agents), and predictable latency for agent UI.
[01:10] Priya: and we have strict SLAs for response under 800 ms p95 for the UI, otherwise agents complain. latency matters more than micro-optimizations of token cost right now.
[01:28] Diego: also data residency — we need logs retained in EU, and keys managed with our KMS. for the poc we can use redwood hosted in eu-west if possible, otherwise dedicated.

[01:45] Maya: noted. so for the POC quality eval playbook i propose 3 primary success criteria: 1) correctness for extraction (we'll measure F1 on a golden set), 2) hallucination rate under X% (we'll define), and 3) latency p95 under 800 ms in pilot config. is that a fair starting point?
[02:08] Amara: yes, F1 is good. for hallucination we typically define as the model inventing an action that isn't supported by the transcript. we need false positive actions at <2% ideally.
[02:30] Ravi: okay low-level — we'll build a golden prompt set for each archetype (short chat, long chat, multi-turn). golden prompts = representative inputs + expected structured output schema. We'll also create augmented negatives (edge cases) to surface hallucinations.
[02:52] Priya: augment how? random perturbations?
[02:55] Ravi: a mix: insert ambiguous language, redact entities, scramble timestamps, simulate truncated contexts. the idea is to stress output slot-filling and see where hallucination appears.

[03:12] Liam: also recommend a regression playlist — the golden set is the ground truth; regression tests are automated runs on that set after any model change or config tweak, with pass/fail thresholds per metric.
[03:30] Amara: what metrics do you suggest for pass/fail? F1 delta? hallucination delta?
[03:34] Maya: yes both. propose: baseline F1 on gold set = 0.87 (example) — we'll set a regression alert at -0.02 absolute drop; hallucination rate must not increase by >0.5 percentage points. both are configurable once we see first run.

[03:54] Diego: what about format checks? Our integration expects a strict JSON schema for actions (fields: action_id, type, confidence, params). if the model deviates formatting we fail downstream. can you validate output schema?
[04:12] Ravi: absolutely — we'll include structural validators in the runner: JSON schema validation, type coercion rules, and confidence calibration checks (e.g., if confidence <0.6 treat as uncertain). we'll also flag partial parses as 'needs human review'.

[04:35] Priya: good. on hallucination detection, do you rely on confidence alone or other signals?
[04:40] Ravi: confidence is useful but not sufficient. we'll use pattern heuristics (e.g., unsupported action types), fuzzy-match against transcript evidence, and token-level attribution heuristics where possible. Redwood runtime supports token-level attribution traces in some models which can help. (brief cough) sometimes the transcript mis-aligned the tokens so we'll call out some noise.

[05:08] Amara: also need to measure partial hallucinations — e.g., correct action type but invented parameter values. that is high risk.
[05:17] Maya: we'll add per-field hallucination metrics: action_type_accuracy, param_accuracy, and a composite 'safe_output' score. scoring approach: weighted F1 with heavier weight on param accuracy. we can share a sample weighting and you can adjust.

[05:36] Diego: for workload sizing for bench runs — we can provide traces but what's your recommended bench?
[05:40] Liam: recommend three bench profiles: 1) Smoke (10k requests total, mix of short/long), 2) Functional (100k requests, 1:5 long:short, concurrency 40), 3) Load (500k requests over 1 hour, sustained 120 rps spike). each will help us size ded pool and estimate p95 latency.
[06:06] Priya: our current average payload is 450 tokens; peaks hit 1200 tokens for long threads. does that change configs?
[06:15] Ravi: yes — sequence length distribution affects kernel selection and memory for KV cache. we'll suggest model variants and quantization profiles. e.g., 8-bit quantization for cost savings but we'll test quality delta on the golden set.

[06:34] Amara: timeline — we want a pilot in production Jan 30. is that realistic?
[06:39] Maya: if we start benchmarking this month, yes. proposed milestones: kickoff now, collect samples and config by Dec 15, first bench run by Dec 22 (hosted), analyze results Dec 23-24, iterate Jan 5 run second benchmark (dedicated fallback), pilot deployment Jan 20-30.
[06:58] Priya: those dates sound tight but possible. Diego will need time to scrub traces.
[07:04] Diego: yes i can anonymize traces by Dec 15.

[07:12] Maya: call out security needs — you mentioned KMS and EU residency. for hosted eu-west we have region isolation; logs can be set to EU retention and we support customer KMS integration via bring-your-own key. any SOC/ISO requirements?
[07:30] Amara: SOC 2 Type II is required. we also will need audit logs and ability to pull model inference audit for a specific customer session.
[07:40] Liam: Redwood can provide audit logs, per-token cost breakdowns, and retention controls; SE will share security pack after the call.

[07:52] Priya: curious about fallback behavior — if latency SLO breaks, can requests fallback to a smaller faster model? we can't risk wrong actions though.
[07:59] Ravi: yes we have smart routing policies — fallback to a smaller model or return cached extraction results, and a canary policy to only fallback for non-critical flows. for critical actions we can fail open to human review instead. We can configure per-route policies.

[08:20] Amara: can you quantify expected cost delta for enabling prefix/KV cache? we want cost/latency trade-offs.
[08:26] Maya: we'll include cost projections in the benchmark spreadsheet — estimate tokens saved with prefix caching and batching. early numbers often show 20–40% per-token cost reduction depending on cache hit rate.

[08:42] Diego: regarding model variants, can we run the same golden set against two model families in parallel? we want apples-to-apples.
[08:49] Ravi: yes we can run parallel model comparisons and give delta reports. we'll produce per-model confusion matrices, per-field error breakdowns, and a composite scorecard.

[09:05] Priya: scoring approach — you mentioned weighted F1 earlier. can we see an example rubric?
[09:12] Maya: yes; quick example rubric included in the sheet we'll send: action_type F1 (weight 0.5), param accuracy (weight 0.35), hallucination penalty (weight -0.2 if above threshold), latency penalty (soft penalty added if p95>800ms). final composite scale 0-100.
[09:34] Amara: will the rubric allow prioritizing certain users or customers? some low-risk flows can tolerate more hallucination.
[09:40] Liam: yes the runner supports tags per example and we can compute segmented metrics by customer tier or channel.

[09:52] Priya: what does the golden prompt creation process look like? we can do a workshop?
[09:57] Maya: yes workshop recommended. Practically: you share 20 seed examples across archetypes, SEs expand to 200 with synthetic augmentations, Solstice reviews and marks critical vs non-critical cases, we finalize gold set. workshop ideally Dec 14.
[10:16] Amara: Dec 14 works for us.

[10:18] Diego: during benchmarks, will you need ephemeral keys to run in our VPC or can we do hosted with logs forwarded to our KMS?
[10:25] Ravi: both options. for fastest turnaround hosted eu-west with BYOK integration is simplest. for dedicated we can coordinate a private endpoint; that will add infra setup time (~1 week).

[10:39] Priya: on regression tests, how often should we run them? nightly? on each model change?
[10:44] Maya: recommended cadence: nightly for smoke checks, and on every model/config deploy for full regression. we'll wire up alerts for drops.

[10:56] Amara: are you able to run hallucination detectors automatically? i.e., flag candidates for human review and estimate how many reviews we'd need?
[11:03] Ravi: yes — we can produce a triage queue with confidence thresholds and estimated human review load. typically for a 12k daily request workload, with strict thresholds, expect 0.5-2% flagged; we'll refine after first run.

[11:18] Priya: going back to format checks: sometimes model returns plural vs singular or missing keys. default should be fail and route to our parser fallback. can we label failures as 'hard fail' vs 'soft fail'?
[11:31] Liam: yes — provide mapping in the runbook. hard fail = break integration, soft fail = attempt best-effort parse and tag for review. We'll include those behaviors in the runner.

[11:44] Diego: can you capture latency breakdowns per-token, per-serialization step? we want to see where time is spent (network, decode, tokenization).
[11:53] Ravi: yes Redwood Console provides that: token-level timelines, per-stage latencies (ingest, model, io). we'll instrument traces for the bench.

[12:05] Maya: let's talk acceptance for pilot: composite score >= 85 and p95 latency <= 800ms on pilot traffic, hallucination <=2% overall and param error <5%. if thresholds not met we either tune or fall back to hybrid approach with human-in-loop for critical flows. does that sound acceptable?
[12:30] Amara: sounds right. one question: you mentioned token attribution traces earlier — are those available for all model families?
[12:36] Ravi: not all. larger open families often support them; proprietary models vary. we'll list per-model capabilities in the benchmark sheet.

[12:46] Priya: for scoring, can you provide per-field confidence calibration? we need to ensure confidence maps to recall/precision trade-offs.
[12:54] Liam: yes we will include calibration plots and suggested thresholds.

[13:06] Maya: quick logistical items: i'll send the golden prompt template and the benchmark spreadsheet after the call. ravi will add instructions for running the runner and the JSON schema for expected outputs. liam will attach the security pack.
[13:20] Amara: thank you. one more thing — training data overlap: we need assurances about training data reuse and privacy.
[13:27] Liam: Redwood does not persist customer prompts to public training corpora and we can opt out of telemetry for your account. we'll include that in security doc.

[13:38] Diego: ok i'll prepare the traces. also, can you include a short plan for model rollback and incident response if a hallucination issue makes it to prod?
[13:48] Ravi: yes, we'll include a rollback runbook and a canary abort threshold (e.g., if hallucination rate >3% for 5 minutes, abort rollout).

[14:00] Priya: does Redwood help prioritize prompts for golden set selection? we have a long tail — which ones should we pick?
[14:06] Maya: pick high-traffic, high-risk, and edge-case examples: 50/30/20 split. we'll guide you in the workshop.

[14:16] Amara: okay good. timeline recap?
[14:20] Maya: kickoff today, workshop Dec 14 to finalize golden set, samples due Dec 15, first hosted benchmark Dec 22, results Dec 23 and tuning through early Jan, pilot deploy Jan 20-30.
[14:34] Priya: sounds good.
[14:36] Diego: noted.

[14:40] Maya: any other questions?
[14:43] Amara: none from me.
[14:45] Priya: no.
[14:46] Diego: all set.

[14:48] Maya: great — recap of action items and who owns them: (see action_items). we'll follow up with calendar invites for the workshop. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
